claims.text: Across the evidence, receiving financial advice in the future is described as combining AI-enabled technology with human advisors to deliver more personalized, holistic, always-on advice across digital and human channels.

Edward Jones states the financial services industry continues to evolve technologically, with more firms providing enhanced digital experiences including artificial intelligence and lower-cost computer-based robo-advice.

According to Capgemini's World Wealth Report, advances in artificial intelligence enable firms to process vast amounts of data and respond to client needs with greater speed and precision, with augmented intelligence enhancing rather than replacing human judgment.
Accenture research reports 96% of surveyed wealth management professionals say AI is transforming how advice is created for, delivered to, and consumed by clients today.

Schwab introduced Charley, a new AI-powered assistant that provides U.S. retail clients with conversational access to Schwab's tools and insights, and partnered with Anthropic to bring Claude for Financial Advisors to the independent RIAs it serves.

Capgemini states that relationship managers will leverage augmented intelligence to orchestrate experiences across the full wealth ecosystem, coordinating specialists in tax, estate planning, lending, philanthropy, and non-financial services.

McKinsey states that replacing tasks is not the same as replacing the advisor's role as the human accountable for judgment, trust, and behavioral coaching, and that winners will keep the human relationship at the front end of trust.
Raymond James' CEO says the firm uses AI to help financial advisors better serve their clients, whereas many competitors use technology to go direct to clients and get around their advisors.

Deloitte states the advice model may shift away from individual effort toward apprenticeship, specialization, and technology leverage, driving more teaming, greater practice consolidation, and a higher premium on leaders who mentor and scale teams.

Capgemini describes an Adaptive Experience AI Engine that dynamically tailors content depth, tone, and engagement pathways based on investor personas and life-event context, enabling journeys to evolve in real time rather than static segmentation.

Deloitte research states that for clients, faster responses, more tailored insights, and more proactive outreach should become minimum standards as agentic AI reshapes how advice is created and delivered.
Schwab's CEO says AI will personalize more journeys and create more opportunities to deepen client relationships over time.

Capgemini's World Wealth Report states the wealth management landscape is shifting from selling products to offering personalized, empathetic advice, with future success defined by how well firms understand clients' lifestyles and aspirations.

McKinsey reports that firms across delivery models are rolling out new advice propositions, with traditionally digital/direct wealth managers rapidly expanding their full-service advice offerings and enhancing the depth and breadth of planning services.
Deloitte predicts agentic AI could lift adviser productivity by roughly 30% to 100% by 2032, freeing 25% to 50% of adviser time from lower-value operational work.

Schwab states its financial consultants use an AI capability that summarizes past client interactions, shares recommended actions, records the meeting, and prepares an action-based summary for the client.

Raymond James launched Rai, a proprietary digital AI operations agent, and lists its AI 360 suite including prudent process reviews, meeting and CRM notes management, client portfolio analyses, and an opportunity dashboard.
Morgan Stanley's early AI use cases include DevGen AI, Parable, and LeadIQ, its AI-powered lead distribution platform matching workplace and self-directed relationships to financial advisors.
Schwab is rolling out an AI-powered thinkorswim assistant and has started a pilot allowing traders to connect to its MCP layer via the LLM of their choice, beginning with Claude.

Cerulli estimates middle-market and mass-affluent households with $100,000 to $2 million in financial assets grew their wealth to a $25 trillion market of 46.9 million households in 2025 that seeks involved advisor relationships.
Capgemini states the future of wealth management will democratize excellence in advice through augmented intelligence across every client interaction.

Schwab states its advisory solutions, including discretionary and non-discretionary services, have minimum investments starting at $5,000, and its retail value proposition combines digital platforms with no minimums or commissions.
Morgan Stanley states it can offer financial advice broadly for different types of individuals at different points in their life cycle and match advisers to the right clients using technology.

Edward Jones states that in its Guided Solutions client-directed advisory program, clients retain control over investment decisions while financial advisors guide them through identifying goals and selecting a portfolio objective.

Capgemini research states engagement models will evolve so life transitions, liquidity events, and behavioral signals determine when and how firms interact with clients, replacing calendar-driven review cycles with relevance-driven ones.
Bank of America states it keeps customers in control of decisions and keeps the human in the loop before money is moved out of their accounts.
McKinsey projects that, based on current trends, US advisor supply will be 290 thousand advisors by 2034, with advisor headcount projected to decline by about 0.2 percent annually.
McKinsey & Co. projects a shortfall of 90,000 to 110,000 advisors by 2034 at current productivity levels.

Bank of America expects headcount to be down by 3,000, or 1.5% year-over-year in 2027, with managers down about 5% while production teammates doing client-facing work are up year-over-year, and its CEO expects 2026 headcount to come down via attrition.
Schwab is continuing to hire financial consultants and wealth advisers in 2026 with about a dozen new branches planned, and planned to hire hundreds of new financial consultants in 2025.
Raymond James ended the fiscal year on 2025-09-30 with a record 8,943 financial advisors, 2% higher than the prior year.
Morgan Stanley's March workforce management action impacted approximately 2% of its global workforce as of 2026-03-31, with $61 million of severance costs in the Wealth Management segment.
Bank of America's investor day deck projects its Private Client Advisors to reach a medium-term target of 700, up from 545 in 3Q25 and 482 in 2019.
